# Reel

> Reel is a native macOS menu bar video downloader. Copy a link, press ⌘V, and it downloads. It runs yt-dlp and ffmpeg locally and is free and open source under the MIT license, with no account, no analytics and no telemetry.

## Facts

- Platform: macOS 14.0 (Sonoma) or later; universal binary (Apple silicon and Intel).
- Price: free. MIT license. No paid tier, no ads.
- Engine: yt-dlp (Unlicense) and ffmpeg, both bundled with the app and updatable in place.
- Install: DMG/zip from GitHub Releases, or `brew install --cask waylake/tap/reel`.
- Latest version: 1.3.2, released 2026-11-07, about 59 MB.
- Updates: Sparkle 2 with EdDSA-signed appcasts. Signed ad-hoc; not notarized by Apple as of 2026-11.
- Interface language: Korean today; the site is English and Korean.
- What it does not do: no DRM circumvention, no accounts, no browser extension, no telemetry.
- Source: https://github.com/waylake/reel

## Pages

- [Home](https://reel.waylake.com/): what Reel is, how the ⌘V workflow works, install options, FAQ.
- [Documentation](https://reel.waylake.com/docs): first launch, failed downloads, YouTube 403 and bot-check errors, cookies, engine updates, file locations, uninstall.
- [Changelog](https://reel.waylake.com/changelog): every release with dates.
- [Privacy](https://reel.waylake.com/privacy): what the app stores and the only two network calls it makes.
- [Licenses](https://reel.waylake.com/licenses): MIT for Reel; yt-dlp, ffmpeg, Sparkle and icon licenses.
- [한국어](https://reel.waylake.com/ko/): the same home page in Korean.

## Common questions

- A download fails with 403 or "The page needs to be reloaded": update the engine in Settings → Advanced → yt-dlp → Update, then retry. YouTube changes its clients often; the yt-dlp update is the fix.
- "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot": an IP-level judgement, not fixed by retrying. Use cookies from a signed-in browser.
- macOS refuses to open the app: it is not notarized. Right-click the app → Open once, or install with Homebrew, which avoids the quarantine prompt.
- Where files go: `~/Movies/Reel` by default; queue at `~/Library/Application Support/Reel/queue.json`.
